title: SEC moves Ole Miss game at Oklahoma to Sunday over Sooners’ ‘strong objection’
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of sports and college teams affected by the FAA nationwide ground stop.

The SEC postponed Ole Miss’ game at Oklahoma to Sunday over the “strong objection” of Sooners athletic director Roger Denny late Friday night, after a nationwide FAA ground stop scrambled travel plans for millions across the country.

The game, originally scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET Saturday at Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., is now scheduled for 1 p.m. ET Sunday on a to-be-announced television network.

Ole Miss did not depart for Norman before Friday’s ground stop, and its contracted charter company could not accommodate a late-night departure afterward, the SEC said in a statement released late Friday night. Instead, the Rebels’ departure was delayed until Saturday afternoon.

In a statement released at the same time as the SEC’s, Denny said Oklahoma objected to the move and agreed to do so only after conference commissioner Greg Sankey told the school it would either play Sunday or forfeit the game.

“Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation. But we’ve been given no other choice,” Denny said in the statement. “We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening.”

Denny said Oklahoma began communicating with Ole Miss and conference officials as soon as it learned of the travel problems Friday.

“We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned,” he said. “But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution.

“After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection.”

Denny also criticized the decision’s impact on fans who had arranged travel, accommodations and plans around the originally scheduled game.

“Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference’s decision tonight,” Denny said.

The FAA halted departures nationwide Friday afternoon after communications problems affected air traffic control centers. The ground stop was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET, more than four hours after it began. Officials warned that travel disruptions would continue as flights resumed.

The stoppage disrupted travel across college football, with No. 2 Utah, No. 6 Texas, No. 8 Tennessee and numerous other programs affected ahead of Saturday’s games. Auburn’s game at Mississippi State was also pushed back, from noon ET to 4:15 p.m. ET Saturday. Other games with adjusted kickoff times included Arizona State-UCF, Baylor-BYU, Utah-Arizona and Washington-Michigan State.

Oklahoma will release additional information Saturday about game logistics and fan appreciation measures, Denny said in the statement.

No. 19 Ole Miss enters the matchup at 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after a 42-7 loss to Georgia. Oklahoma is 5-4 and 3-3 in the conference following a 23-7 win at Florida. The Rebels have won all three meetings between the programs, including a 34-26 victory in Norman last season.
